# Linear regression sample size calculation for test of overall model significance
# H0: ρ² = 0 vs H1: ρ² ≠ 0
# Test: F = [R²/k] / [(1-R²)/(n-k-1)]
# Noncentrality parameter: λ = R²(n-k-1) / (1-R²)

library(stats)

# Parameters
r_squared <- 0.30          # Population R-squared (anticipated multiple correlation)
k <- 3                      # Number of predictors
alpha <- 0.05              # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90       # Target power

# Critical value for two-sided test at alpha = 0.05
# For overall F test: df1 = k, df2 = n - k - 1
# Critical value depends on n, so we'll iterate

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size n
calculate_power_linear <- function(n, r_sq, k, alpha) {
  if (n <= k) return(0)  # Invalid design
  
  df1 <- k                    # numerator df
  df2 <- n - k - 1            # denominator df
  
  # Critical value for two-sided test
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- r_sq * (n - k - 1) / (1 - r_sq)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size giving power >= 0.90
# Start with a reasonable range
n_search <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(n_search, function(n) calculate_power_linear(n, r_squared, k, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target
idx_sufficient <- which(powers >= target_power)

if (length(idx_sufficient) > 0) {
  n_min <- n_search[idx_sufficient[1]]
  power_achieved <- powers[idx_sufficient[1]]
  
  # Also report power at the preceding sample size
  if (n_min > 10) {
    n_preceding <- n_min - 1
    power_preceding <- calculate_power_linear(n_preceding, r_squared, k, alpha)
  } else {
    n_preceding <- NA
    power_preceding <- NA
  }
} else {
  n_min <- NA
  power_achieved <- NA
  n_preceding <- NA
  power_preceding <- NA
}

# Detailed calculation for minimum sample size
cat("=== Linear Regression Power Analysis ===\n")
cat("Hypothesis: H₀: ρ² = 0 vs. H₁: ρ² ≠ 0\n")
cat("Test: Noncentral F distribution\n")
cat("Alpha (two-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Number of predictors (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Anticipated R-squared:", r_squared, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

cat("Results:\n")
cat("Minimum total sample size:", n_min, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_min, ":", sprintf("%.6f", power_achieved), "\n")
if (!is.na(n_preceding)) {
  cat("Power at n =", n_preceding, ":", sprintf("%.6f", power_preceding), "\n")
}

# Verify the calculation step-by-step for n_min
if (!is.na(n_min)) {
  cat("\n=== Verification for n =", n_min, "===\n")
  df1 <- k
  df2 <- n_min - k - 1
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)
  lambda <- r_squared * (n_min - k - 1) / (1 - r_squared)
  power_check <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  cat("Numerator df (df1):", df1, "\n")
  cat("Denominator df (df2):", df2, "\n")
  cat("Critical F-value:", sprintf("%.6f", f_crit), "\n")
  cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", sprintf("%.6f", lambda), "\n")
  cat("Power (verification):", sprintf("%.6f", power_check), "\n")
}

# Return final results
result <- list(
  sample_size = n_min,
  power_achieved = power_achieved,
  sample_size_preceding = n_preceding,
  power_preceding = power_preceding
)

cat("\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_min, unit = "participants_total"),
  list(metric = "power_achieved", value = round(power_achieved, 6), unit = "probability"),
  list(metric = "sample_size_preceding", value = if(is.na(n_preceding)) NULL else n_preceding, unit = "participants_total"),
  list(metric = "power_preceding", value = if(is.na(power_preceding)) NULL else round(power_preceding, 6), unit = "probability")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Linear regression sample size calculation for test of overall model significance
# H0: ρ² = 0 vs H1: ρ² ≠ 0
# Test: F = [R²/k] / [(1-R²)/(n-k-1)]
# Noncentrality parameter: λ = R²(n-k-1) / (1-R²)

library(stats)

# Parameters
r_squared <- 0.30          # Population R-squared (anticipated multiple correlation)
k <- 3                      # Number of predictors
alpha <- 0.05              # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90       # Target power

# Critical value for two-sided test at alpha = 0.05
# For overall F test: df1 = k, df2 = n - k - 1
# Critical value depends on n, so we'll iterate

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size n
calculate_power_linear <- function(n, r_sq, k, alpha) {
  if (n <= k) return(0)  # Invalid design
  
  df1 <- k                    # numerator df
  df2 <- n - k - 1            # denominator df
  
  # Critical value for two-sided test
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- r_sq * (n - k - 1) / (1 - r_sq)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size giving power >= 0.90
# Start with a reasonable range
n_search <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(n_search, function(n) calculate_power_linear(n, r_squared, k, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target
idx_sufficient <- which(powers >= target_power)

if (length(idx_sufficient) > 0) {
  n_min <- n_search[idx_sufficient[1]]
  power_achieved <- powers[idx_sufficient[1]]
  
  # Also report power at the preceding sample size
  if (n_min > 10) {
    n_preceding <- n_min - 1
    power_preceding <- calculate_power_linear(n_preceding, r_squared, k, alpha)
  } else {
    n_preceding <- NA
    power_preceding <- NA
  }
} else {
  n_min <- NA
  power_achieved <- NA
  n_preceding <- NA
  power_preceding <- NA
}

# Detailed calculation for minimum sample size
cat("=== Linear Regression Power Analysis ===\n")
cat("Hypothesis: H₀: ρ² = 0 vs. H₁: ρ² ≠ 0\n")
cat("Test: Noncentral F distribution\n")
cat("Alpha (two-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Number of predictors (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Anticipated R-squared:", r_squared, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

cat("Results:\n")
cat("Minimum total sample size:", n_min, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_min, ":", sprintf("%.6f", power_achieved), "\n")
if (!is.na(n_preceding)) {
  cat("Power at n =", n_preceding, ":", sprintf("%.6f", power_preceding), "\n")
}

# Verify the calculation step-by-step for n_min
if (!is.na(n_min)) {
  cat("\n=== Verification for n =", n_min, "===\n")
  df1 <- k
  df2 <- n_min - k - 1
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)
  lambda <- r_squared * (n_min - k - 1) / (1 - r_squared)
  power_check <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)

  cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", sprintf("%.6f", lambda), "\n")
  cat("Power (verification):", sprintf("%.6f", power_check), "\n")

  if (n <= k) return(0)  # Invalid design

  df2 <- n - k - 1            # denominator df

  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)

# Noncentrality parameter: λ = R²(n-k-1) / (1-R²)

library(stats)

# Parameters
r_squared <- 0.30          # Population R-squared (anticipated multiple correlation)
k <- 3                      # Number of predictors
alpha <- 0.05              # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90       # Target power

# Critical value for two-sided test at alpha = 0.05
# For overall F test: df1 = k, df2 = n - k - 1
# Critical value depends on n, so we'll iterate

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size n
calculate_power_linear <- function(n, r_sq, k, alpha) {
  if (n <= k) return(0)  # Invalid design
  
  df1 <- k                    # numerator df
  df2 <- n - k - 1            # denominator df
  
  # Critical value for two-sided test
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- r_sq * (n - k - 1) / (1 - r_sq)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size giving power >= 0.90
# Start with a reasonable range
n_search <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(n_search, function(n) calculate_power_linear(n, r_squared, k, alpha))
